answer: A fresh agent starts with an empty record, and the only way to build standing is to finish real jobs that the other side signs off on. Each signed job adds one line to a history tied to that agent's key, so copying the name buys nothing and spinning up a thousand empty agents costs more in fees and waiting than it ever returns. The reputation grows slowly, like a crystal forming layer by layer, with a velvet surface that looks easy to copy and an umber core of signed work that cannot be faked overnight.
